body:
> this is fixed by #3324 right?

3324 was about update. This is select. In this case are unknown properties removed without error.
ah, okay... Shall we apply same strategy for selects?

Original question:
> Is there any reason the `doesNotExist` is not present in the resulting SQL query please?

@realyze if typeorm do not remove non-exists columns from your query, you will get error from database. So thats reason why we do it.

> ah, okay... Shall we apply same strategy for selects?

This is breaking change. Lot of users will get errors after it. But IMHO it is correct behaviour to throw error if someone try to use unknown column in where statement of SQL (database will return error in this case, too). @Kononnable, @havenchyk what do you think about this?
Im for throwing an error. If its so-breaking we need to do it against `next`.

Just got the same thing - thought that the field was used in the query, but it was just skipped :{

Will be great to throw an error.
How about adding a flag that toggles between the new/old behaviour? IMO the default should be to throw (because of principle of least surprise) but it would be good to allow users to opt out.
also here are old issues for this #2528, #2690

**Steps to reproduce or a small repository showing the problem:**

```ts
class User {
    Email!: string;
}
```

```ts
class export class UserRepository extends AbstractRepository<User> {
    public getByEmail(mail: string): Promise<User | undefined> {
        return this.repository.findOne({where: { Email: mail }});
    }
}
```

This works es expected.
```sql
query: SELECT ... FROM `user` `User` WHERE `User`.`email` = ? -- PARAMETERS: ["u1@test.test"]
```

However if I change the Email in the where clause to email or anything different the query is executed without the where clause.

```ts
        return this.repository.findOne({where: { email: mail }});
        return this.repository.findOne({where: { x: mail }});
```
```sql
query: SELECT ... FROM `user` `User`
```

Shouldn't this throw an exception of missing columns instead?

body: I still think this is **highly critical**. This bug causes delete/update statements to drop/update more data than the query would assume.

Very often it happens like this: `where: { userId }` instead of `where: { user }`.
It can be really hard to find this out during a code review.
I think it should just throw an error as well. This kind of error is very difficult to be checked during code review.
Okey, I think we should add this into 0.3.0 release as throwing error is breaking change for som users.
Would it be possible to get a config switch or something alike for this in the next release? This is really dangerous behaviour imho.

Like @spech66 mentioned, the current behaviour is very dangerous, because intentionally one would think that queries are correct when there is no error. If I query "Tasks by user" and the user field is misspelled (or has been changed), then TypeORM is leaking ALL data.

Finding a solution for this would be great 👍
